subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename bootstrap files as a core hook contract, or keep bootstrap-extra-files limited to recognized workspace filenames?
rationale: The current source and docs intentionally limit injected bootstrap extras to known filenames, while the requested behavior expands deterministic system-prompt context loading and possibly adds or changes user-facing hook config semantics.

options.title: Approve Repaired Hook Contract
options.body: Allow custom-basename files through the existing hook path after the linked PR or replacement is rebased and preserves path guards, budgets, docs, diagnostics, and session filtering.

options.title: Keep Recognized Basenames Only
options.body: Reject arbitrary workspace-file injection and keep custom context in first-class workspace filenames or on-demand file reads.

options.title: Defer To Broader Context Design
options.body: Leave this request open or supersede it only when maintainers choose a broader context/config API that covers custom startup files.

recommendation.title: Approve Repaired Hook Contract
recommendation.body: Allow custom-basename files through the existing hook path after the linked PR or replacement is rebased and preserves path guards, budgets, docs, diagnostics, and session filtering.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the hook refactor and is the strongest current routing signal for the bootstrap hook contract decision.
